title: Interrupted prune deletes the only archive of audit rows it has already committed as pruned
description: retention.prune writes the archive, then deletes the audit and approval rows and records an anchor holding the archive's sha256 in one transaction. Its outer error handler unlinks the archive on any BaseException without checking whether that transaction committed. A Ctrl-C (SIGINT) that arrives while the fsync-bound COMMIT runs is raised by CPython right after COMMIT returns, still inside the inner try. The handler's ROLLBACK then fails with 'no transaction is active', and the outer handler deletes the archive. Result: the DB says rows 1..N were pruned into an archive with a recorded sha256, that archive no longer exists, verify() reports the chain intact ('pruned through #N'), and verify_archives can never pass again. The pruned audit history and its tamper evidence are gone for good, which breaks the stated invariant that a failed prune leaves the database and archive consistent.
root_cause: The cleanup in retention.py:130-131 (`except BaseException: archive.unlink(missing_ok=True)`) is keyed on 'an exception happened' rather than 'the prune transaction did not commit'. The inner handler (retention.py:127-129) runs ROLLBACK unconditionally even when conn.in_transaction is already False after a successful COMMIT (retention.py:126). Any exception that surfaces after COMMIT completes, such as KeyboardInterrupt delivered during COMMIT, therefore destroys the archive that the committed anchor (retention.py:118-121) refers to.
intended_behavior: The archive is removed only if the prune transaction did not commit. Once the anchor row referencing the archive's sha256 is durable, the archive must be kept whatever exception follows, and the failure must be reported as 'pruned; archive kept at <path>'.

trace.description: Host operator runs `agentbox prune --before ... --archive ...`, which calls retention.prune on Settings().db_path.
The archive is written, fsynced, and its sha256 computed before the transaction.
Inside BEGIN IMMEDIATE, audit rows are deleted and an audit_anchor row with the archive name and sha256 is inserted.
COMMIT makes the deletion and anchor durable. A SIGINT pending during this call is raised as KeyboardInterrupt immediately after it returns, still inside the inner try.
Unconditional ROLLBACK raises OperationalError('cannot rollback - no transaction is active'), which chains on the KeyboardInterrupt.
archive.unlink deletes the only copy of the rows the committed anchor says were archived.

evidence.description: The archive is unlinked on any BaseException with no check of commit state.
ROLLBACK is issued without checking conn.in_transaction, so it raises after a successful COMMIT.
verify() starts at the latest anchor, so it keeps passing after the archive is lost and hides the loss.
verify_archives needs the archive whose sha256 the anchor holds. With it deleted, full-history verification is impossible from then on.
cmd_prune catches only ValueError/FileExistsError/RuntimeError. The OperationalError surfaces as a traceback, and a re-run reports nothing to prune.

conditions.description: Host operator running the prune CLI with direct DB file access. No remote or agent principal is involved.

SIGINT (Ctrl-C or a supervisor such as `timeout -s INT`) arrives while COMMIT executes, or in the few bytecodes after it inside the inner try. COMMIT of a large prune is fsync-bound (about 0.27 s for 20k 1 KB rows in the sandbox, longer on large production DBs).
At least one audit row is older than the cutoff, so prune reaches the transaction.

execution.attacker_perspective: Operator mistake the code claims to handle (interrupted prune). No adversary is needed. The effect is loss of audit-log integrity evidence for the pruned range.
payloads: h.py check1: AuditLog fixture with 5 rows before the cutoff and 2 after; retention.sqlite3 shimmed to a Connection subclass whose execute('COMMIT') calls the real COMMIT and then signal.raise_signal(SIGINT); prune(db, cut, 'c1.jsonl.gz')

h2.py: WAL DB, synchronous=FULL, BEGIN IMMEDIATE + 20000 randomblob(1000) inserts; threading.Timer(dur/3) sends os.kill(getpid(), SIGINT) during a real COMMIT inside the same nested try/except layout as retention.prune
instructions: Run tools/sbx h-retention /usr/bin/python3.13 /scratch/h.py (no network, read-only /target, uid 65534, 512 MiB, 120 s) and read check1 output.
Run tools/sbx h-retention /usr/bin/python3.13 /scratch/h2.py to show that a real asynchronous SIGINT during a real COMMIT surfaces in the inner except after the commit is durable.
execution.observed_result: check1: prune raised OperationalError, context KeyboardInterrupt. Archive exists after failure: False. Audit table now holds rows 6-8 with anchor (seq 1, last_id 5, 'c1.jsonl.gz', sha 3628529612...). verify(): ok=True, pruned_through=5. verify_archives([archive]) raised FileNotFoundError; verify_archives([]) returned ok=False ('anchor count 1, archives 0'). h2: 5/5 attempts gave inner-except KeyboardInterrupt, then ROLLBACK raised 'cannot rollback - no transaction is active', then the outer except ran, with 20000 rows committed.

remediation.strategy: Make archive cleanup depend on the DB's commit state, not on whether an exception was raised. Roll back only while a transaction is active. Before unlinking, check whether the anchor for this archive's sha256 exists, and keep the archive if it does. Also fsync the parent directory after creating the archive so the anchor never outlives its archive's directory entry after a crash. Regression test: a Connection factory that raises KeyboardInterrupt after a successful COMMIT must leave the archive in place, and verify_archives([archive]) must pass.

likelihood.reason: Requires the operator (or a supervisor) to send SIGINT during the COMMIT of a host-only CLI command. The window is short but real for large prunes, which are the intended use (disk pressure), and Ctrl-C on a slow-looking command is a common operator action.

impact.reason: The only remaining copy of the pruned audit rows (and finished approvals) is permanently destroyed, while the in-DB anchor and verify() report the history as cleanly archived. Tamper evidence for the whole pruned range becomes unverifiable from then on. No confidentiality impact and no remote attacker.

confidence.reason: Source path is direct. The end-to-end prune harness reproduced archive deletion after commit, and a real asynchronous SIGINT during a real COMMIT surfaced in the inner except in 5 of 5 runs on CPython 3.13.
